paragraph: Angola's standards body, the Instituto Nacional da Qualidade e Infra-estruturas, is listed on [ISO's member register as a correspondent member](<https://www.iso.org/member/316519.html>), on a page read in August 2026. The register shows it observing on technical committees and on ISO's policy development committees, and names none of them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names an international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Burundi's standards body, the Bureau Burundais de Normalisation et Contrôle de la Qualité, is listed on [ISO's member page, read on 16 October 2026, as Burundi's ISO member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1591.html>). The page shows it holding 11 participating and 28 observing seats on technical committees, and names none of them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No rule requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Benin's Agence nationale de Normalisation, de Métrologie et du Contrôle Qualité is listed on [ISO's member register as a member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/308845.html>), on a page read in August 2026. A [decree of 2017](<https://sgg.gouv.bj/doc/decret-2017-031/download>) set up the agency to represent Benin in international standards bodies. In the last twelve months, in 2026, the digital agency [recommended three international standards](<https://asin.bj/doc/137/download>) on information security, privacy and artificial intelligence. They are for public servants using generative AI tools. That is advice, and no international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Burkina Faso's standards body, the Agence Burkinabè de Normalisation, de Métrologie et de la Qualité (ABNORM), is listed on [ISO's member register as the country's member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/269997.html>), on a page read on 16 October 2026. In the last twelve months, [the participation page of ISO/IEC JTC 1](<http://iso.org/committee/45020.html?view=participation>), captured in May 2026, lists ABNORM as a participating member. JTC 1 is the joint committee of ISO and IEC that writes information technology standards. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. Nothing found shows a requirement on public bodies. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Cote d'Ivoire's standards body, CODINORM, is listed on [ISO's member register as a member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1674.html>), the full class of membership, on a page read in 2026. In the last twelve months, [the participation page of ISO/IEC JTC 1](<http://iso.org/committee/45020.html?view=participation>), captured in May 2026, lists CODINORM as a participating member. JTC 1 is the joint committee of ISO and IEC that writes information technology standards. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No rule requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Cameroon's standards body, the Agence des Normes et de la Qualité (ANOR), is listed on [ISO's member page, read in October 2026, as Cameroon's ISO member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1623.html>). The same page says the agency is a member of the IEC, the International Electrotechnical Commission. It shows the agency participating in 4 ISO technical committees and observing 41, and names none of them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No rule requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo's standards body, the Office Congolais de Controle (OCC), is listed on [ISO's member page as the country's ISO member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/308894.html>), on a page dated 2026. In April 2024 the office [presented itself as a member of ISO and of the IEC affiliate country programme](<https://www.occ.cd/2024/04/25/participation-de-locc-a-la-8eme-edition-de-la-semaine-francaise-de-kinshasa/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No rule requiring public bodies to meet one has been found, nor a seat on an ISO or IEC committee. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Congo's standards body, the Agence Congolaise de Normalisation et de la Qualité (ACONOQ), is listed on [ISO's member page, dated 16 October 2026, as a member body of ISO](<https://www.iso.org/member/11493926.html>) and as an Affiliate Plus member of the IEC. [Law 19-2015 of 29 October 2015](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/Con179594.pdf>) set the agency up. The page shows it in 2 ISO technical committees and 3 project committees. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Djibouti's standards body, the Agence Djiboutienne des Normes et de la Qualité (ADN), is listed on [ISO's member register as a correspondent member](<https://www.iso.org/member/10466380.html>), on a page read in 2026. In August 2024 the daily La Nation [reported that the agency had formally joined ISO and the International Organization of Legal Metrology](<https://www.lanation.dj/adhesion-de-lagence-djiboutienne-des-normes-et-de-la-qualite-a-liso-et-a-loiml-un-pas-decisif-pour-lamelioration-des-normes-nationales-des-produits-et-services/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No rule requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Algeria's Institut Algérien de Normalisation (IANOR) is listed on [ISO's member page as Algeria's member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1499.html>), as read in November 2026, with 27 participating and 50 observing committee seats. In the last twelve months, IANOR's [draft programme for 2026](<https://www.ianor.dz/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/PROJET-DE-PROGRAMME-NATIONAL-DE-NORMALISATION-2026.pdf>) listed the national standard NA ISO/IEC 14651, numbered NA 13037, for revision to ISO/IEC 14651:2025. That standard sets how software orders text. No rule has been found that requires public bodies to meet a named international standard. Operating would need a legal text that names an international standard on information technology or data and binds public bodies.

Egypt's standards body, the Egyptian Organization for Standardization and Quality (EOS), is listed on [ISO's member page as an ISO member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1700.html>), with ISO membership obtained in 1957. [The IEC members page lists Egypt as a Full Member](<https://iec.ch/dyn/www/f?p=103%3A33%3A0%3A%3A%3A%3AFSP_ORG_ID%3A1044>) in 2026. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No requirement on public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Eritrea's standards body, the Eritrean Standards Institution (ESI), is listed on [ISO's member page, dated 2026, as a correspondent member of ISO](<https://www.iso.org/member/318778.html>). A correspondent member is listed by ISO but is not one of its participating members. The page names no seat on a committee writing standards. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No law or circular requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Ethiopia's standards body, the Institute of Ethiopian Standards, is listed on [ISO's member register as a member body of ISO and as an associate member of IEC](<https://www.iso.org/member/1725.html>) in 2026. The same register page is the only source found on the country's standing. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. Nothing found shows a law, decree or circular requiring public bodies to meet one, or a seat on an ISO or IEC committee. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Gabon's standards body, the Agence Gabonaise de Normalisation (AGANOR), is listed on [ISO's member page as Gabon's member](<https://www.iso.org/member/548909.html>), taking part in three technical committees, on a page read in 2026. The page does not name the committees, and no source found says whether any concerns information technology or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No rule requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

The IEC National Committee of Ghana [says Ghana holds Associate Member status in the IEC](<https://iecncgh.org/international-affiliations/>) in 2026. In the last twelve months, [the participation page of ISO/IEC JTC 1](<http://iso.org/committee/45020.html?view=participation>), captured in May 2026, lists Ghana's GSA as a participating member of the parent committee. JTC 1 is the joint committee of ISO and IEC that writes information technology standards. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No law, circular or procurement rule requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

No stage is set. In the last twelve months, a transport ministry order of 25 June 2026 [required the national passenger-data system](<https://newsaero.info/fr/article/institutions/guinee-api-pnr-donnees-passagers-washington>) to run in a state-approved data centre, with security conforming to ISO/IEC 27001. It is a rule for one sector. No source found names the standards body as a member of ISO or IEC, or says it belongs to neither. Preparing would need a source showing the country's standards body to be a member of ISO or IEC, in any class of membership.

The Gambia Standards Bureau is listed on [ISO's member register as a correspondent member](<https://www.iso.org/member/576505.html>), on a page read in September 2026. Its [2022 catalogue of national standards](<https://tgsb.gm/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/TGSB-STANDARDS-CATALOGUE-2022.pdf>) lists GAMS ISO/IEC 27001:2005, on information security management systems, as a Gambian Standard. A 2025 report says the national cybersecurity strategy for 2022 to 2026 [suggests the international information security standards for government agencies](<https://dco.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Gambia-Report.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No law, decree, regulation, directive or circular requiring public bodies to meet a named standard has been found. Operating would need a legal text that names an international standard on information technology or data and binds public bodies.

Kenya's standards body, the Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS), is listed on [ISO's member registry as a member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1854.html>), on a page read in October 2026. The page shows KEBS participating on 129 technical committees and does not say which cover information technology or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national standard on information technology or data taken from an international one has been found. No law, decree or circular requiring public bodies to meet a named international standard has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

The Liberia Standards Authority gained correspondent membership of ISO, according to [its statement of 7 October 2025](<https://frontpageafricaonline.com/liberia-standards-authority-joins-iso-afsec-as-director-general-departs-for-global-leaders-gathering-in-rwanda/>). In November 2025 its director general [announced that Liberia is now a full member of ISO](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/news/liberia-attains-full-iso-membership/article_31c242b3-2a0f-4118-b019-581fea289693.html>). In November 2026 [ISO's own member page listed the authority as a correspondent member](<https://www.iso.org/member/11464839.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Libya's standards body, the Libyan National Centre for Standardization and Metrology (LNCSM), is listed on [ISO's member page as Libya's ISO member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1890.html>), on a page dated 2026. The page names no technical committee in which the centre takes part. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No rule requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Morocco's standards body, the Institut Marocain de Normalisation (IMANOR), is listed on [ISO's member page as Morocco's ISO member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1931.html>) in 2026, the full class of membership. The page names no ISO or IEC committee on information technology or data where Morocco is a member, chair or secretariat. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No law or circular requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Madagascar's standards body, the Bureau des Normes de Madagascar, [says Madagascar joined ISO through it and holds correspondent member status](<https://www.bnm.mg/participation-de-madagascar-a-la-reunion-annuelle-2024-de-liso-a-carthagene-des-indes-colombie/>); two of its staff attended ISO's General Assembly in September 2024. A United Nations Development Programme assessment of December 2025 [also names the bureau a correspondent member of ISO](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2025-12/dra_final_report_madagascar_vf_0.pdf>). It says public information shows no programme of standards on artificial intelligence or data governance. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Mali's standards body, the Agence Malienne de Normalisation et de Promotion de la Qualité (AMANORM), is listed on [ISO's member register as a member body](<https://www.iso.org/fr/member/1915.html>), the full class of membership, on a page read in September 2026. The register adds that the agency belongs to the West African programme for harmonising standards. It shows participating and observing seats on technical committees and names none of them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Mozambique's standards body, the Instituto Nacional de Normalização e Qualidade (INNOQ), is listed on [ISO's member page as a correspondent member of ISO](<https://www.iso.org/member/1978.html>), on a page read in 2026. The page shows the institute participating in 5 technical committees and observing 9 more, and names none of them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. No law, decree or circular requiring public bodies to meet a named international standard has been found either. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Mauritania's standards body, the Office National de la Normalisation et de la Métrologie (ONANOR), is listed on [ISO's member page as Mauritania's correspondent member](<https://www.iso.org/member/576513.html>), on a page read in October 2026. The page shows it taking part in 5 ISO technical committees and observing 10 more, and names none of the 15. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No rule binding public bodies to a named standard has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

The Mauritius Standards Bureau is listed on [ISO's member page as the country's member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1944.html>), as read in November 2026. The page shows 34 participating and 28 observing committee seats. Under Government Notice 119 of 25 January 2025 it [published five ISO/IEC standards as Mauritian Standards](<https://msb.intnet.mu/Documents/Standards/Published%20Mauritian%20Standards/Published%20Mauritian%20Standards%20in%202025.pdf>). They cover artificial intelligence, its risk and governance, and cybersecurity. In the last twelve months, the bureau's [register at 30 June 2026](<https://msb.intnet.mu/Documents/Certification-Schemes/General/Registered%20firms/Attachment%202%20-%20List%20of%20registered%20firms%20ISMS%2030-06-2026.pdf>) lists 11 organisations certified to MS ISO/IEC 27001:2022. No rule requiring public bodies to meet a named standard has been found. Operating would need a legal text that names an international standard on information technology or data and binds public bodies.

Malawi's standards body, the Malawi Bureau of Standards, is listed on [ISO's member page as Malawi's ISO member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1921.html>), on a page dated 2026. The page shows the bureau taking part in 13 technical committees of ISO and does not say which they are. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No law or rule requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Namibia's standards body, the Namibian Standards Institution, is listed on [ISO's member page as a member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1569.html>), taking part in 21 technical committees, as read in October 2026. The page names none of them as a committee on information technology. In the last twelve months, the [Electronic Signature Regulations of December 2025](<https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2025/8814.pdf>), made under the Electronic Transactions Act, 2019, defined the ITU-T X.509 and ISO/IEC 9594-8 standards for electronic signatures. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No rule requiring public bodies to meet one has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Niger's standards body, the Agence Nigérienne de Normalisation, de Métrologie et de Certification (ANMC), is listed on [ISO's member register as a correspondent member](<https://www.iso.org/member/326615.html>) in 2026. That is the class of membership for countries that follow ISO's work without taking part in writing its standards. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. No law or decree requiring ministries to meet one has been found. Nor has a seat for the agency on an ISO or IEC committee on the subject. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Nigeria's standards body, the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), is listed on [ISO's member page as Nigeria's ISO member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/1982.html>), as read in 2026, with 109 technical committees. In the last twelve months, [the participation page of ISO/IEC JTC 1](<http://iso.org/committee/45020.html?view=participation>), captured in May 2026, lists SON as a participating member. JTC 1 is the joint committee that writes information technology standards. No source found says which international standards on information technology or data Nigeria has taken up. None says whether any public body must meet one. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

The Rwanda Standards Board [lists participating membership of 28 ISO technical committees](<https://www.rsb.gov.rw/standards/our-technical-committees/rsb-technical-committees/international-and-regional-technical-committees>), on its own page read in October 2026. The same page lists Rwanda as a participating member of ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 40, the committee on IT service management and IT governance. It lists Rwanda as an observer on JTC 1 and on SC 27, the subcommittee on information security. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national standard taken from an international one has been found, and no rule requiring public bodies to meet one. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Sudan's standards body, the Sudanese Standards and Metrology Organization (SSMO), is listed on [ISO's member page as Sudan's member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/2078.html>), as read in November 2026, and as an affiliate member of IEC. SSMO's [catalogue of Sudanese Standards](<https://www.ssmo.gov.sd/Content/SectorDetails/783020af-a1ce-46f5-aaa1-525dd82ca005>) lists Sudanese Standard 4469:2018, on printer toner yield, as equivalent to ISO 19752:2017. It lists 1633-1:2015, on metadata for records, as equivalent to ISO 23081-1:2006. In the last twelve months, the central bank issued a [cybersecurity framework](<https://cbos.gov.sd/sites/default/files/document.pdf>) in January 2026 for banks. It binds one sector, not ministries or agencies. Operating would need a legal text that names an international standard on information technology or data and binds public bodies.

Senegal's standards body, the Association Sénégalaise de Normalisation, says in its [2025 catalogue of Senegalese standards](<https://asn.sn/sites/default/files/ASN%20CATALOGUE%202025%20v2_0.pdf>) that it holds every ISO standard in its database as the national member organisation of ISO. The catalogue does not give the class of membership. It lists Senegalese standards by field and names no seat on an international committee. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

The Sierra Leone Standards Bureau is listed on [ISO's member page, read in October 2026, as a correspondent member of ISO](<https://www.iso.org/member/576517.html>) since 1 January 2009. The same page lists it as an affiliate of IEC, ISO's counterpart for electrical technology. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. No law, regulation or circular requiring public bodies to meet one has been found, nor an ISO or IEC committee seat on information technology. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

The Somali Bureau of Standards is listed on [ISO's member register as a member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/8867946.html>), the full class of membership, on a page read in August 2026. In May 2023 the US International Trade Administration [described the bureau as an ISO member and an IEC affiliate](<https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/somalia-trade-standards>). In the last twelve months, in June 2026, Somalia issued a [national cybersecurity risk management framework](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/07/21/somalia-launches-national-cybersecurity-risk-management-framework/>). It takes two international information security standards as its guide. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

The Service National de la Propriété Intellectuelle et de la Qualité (SENAPIQ-STP) is the standards body of São Tomé and Príncipe. [ISO's member directory lists it as a correspondent member](<https://www.iso.org/member/7310132.html>), on a page read in 2026. The entry lists no seat on a technical committee. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national standard, and no international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national one, has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

The Eswatini Standards Authority (ESWASA) is listed on [ISO's member page as a correspondent member of ISO](<https://www.iso.org/member/304927.html>), as read in November 2026. The same page names Eswatini an affiliate member of IEC. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the authority [launched the National Addressing Standards](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/eswatini-standards-authority_improvingtheworldwelivein-eswasa-nationaladdressing-activity-7484866707195322368-8UQ2>), SZNS ISO 19160 parts 1 and 2. Its [information technology catalogue](<https://estore.swasa.co.sz/product-category/information-technology/>) lists ISO standards on Dublin Core metadata and on records management as national standards. No rule binding ministries or agencies has been found. Operating would need a legal text that names an international standard on information technology or data and binds public bodies.

The Seychelles Bureau of Standards is listed on [ISO's member page as an ISO member](<https://www.iso.org/member/2084.html>) in 2026, and the page does not state the class of membership. It shows the bureau observing 21 technical committees and 3 policy development committees, and names none of them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. Nothing found shows the bureau chairing or writing for a committee, or a rule requiring public bodies to meet an international standard. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Chad's standards body, the Agence Tchadienne de Normalisation (ATNOR), is listed on [ISO's member page as a correspondent member](<https://www.iso.org/member/8042280.html>), on a page dated 2026. The page shows it observing 7 technical committees and 2 policy development committees, and names none of them. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, the agency [signed a cooperation protocol with AFNOR](<https://manara.td/normalisation-latnor-et-lafnor-scellent-un-partenariat-strategique-a-paris/>). The partnership is meant to align Chad's standardisation on international standards. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Togo's standards body, the Agence Togolaise de Normalisation, is listed on [ISO's member register as a member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/2143.html>), the full class of membership, on a page read in September 2026. The entry places the agency under the ministry for the promotion of investment, in Lomé. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Tunisia's standards body, INNORPI, is listed on [ISO's registry entry, read on 16 October 2026, as Tunisia's ISO member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/2158.html>). In January 2025 the head of government [said INNORPI was Tunisia's official representative at ISO](<https://www.lapresse.tn/2025/01/14/la-tunisie-renforce-ses-liens-avec-liso-pour-un-avenir-technologique-et-durable/>), recently elected to the ISO board for 2024 to 2026. A [2009 law on the national standardisation system](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/tun93198.pdf>) governs national standardisation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Tanzania's standards body, the Tanzania Bureau of Standards, is listed on [ISO's member page as a member body of ISO](<https://www.iso.org/member/2120.html>), on a page dated 2026. The page shows it as a participating member of 42 ISO technical committees and an observing member of 148 others. It does not say which deal with information technology or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No international standard on information technology or data has been found adopted nationally. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

Uganda's standards body, the Uganda National Bureau of Standards, is listed on [ISO's member page as Uganda's ISO member](<https://www.iso.org/member/308866.html>), as read in April 2025. In the last twelve months, on 15 July 2026, the National Information Technology Authority launched [the National Information Security Policy 2026](<https://www.nita.go.ug/sites/default/files/2026-07/Updated-National%20Information%20Security%20Framework%20(NISF).pdf>). It sets mandatory requirements for ministries, departments, agencies and local governments, including ISO/IEC 27001:2022 for their cloud, interface and artificial intelligence systems. The policy cites international standards but does not make them national ones. No adopted Uganda Standard on information technology or data has been found. Establishing would need a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology or data adopted nationally.

South Africa's standards body, SABS, [takes part in ISO/IEC JTC 1](<https://www.iso.org/member/1485.html?t=PT&view=participation>), the joint committee on information technology. It also takes part in the subcommittees on information security, biometrics and artificial intelligence. South Africa was listed among the participating members at [the committee's plenary in Chengdu in November 2025](<https://jtc1info.org/sd-2-history/jtc-1-plenaries/jtc-1-plenary-50/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names an international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard. Nor has a rule been found that requires public bodies to meet one. Establishing would need an international standard adopted as a national one.

No stage is set. [The ISO/IEC JTC 1 participation page](<http://iso.org/committee/45020.html?view=participation>), captured in May 2026, lists Zambia's ZABS as a participating member of the joint committee that writes information technology standards. In the last twelve months, that page is the only source found on the body's place in international standards work. Nothing found names the country's standards body as a member of ISO or IEC, and nothing says it belongs to neither. Preparing would need a source showing the standards body to be a member of ISO or IEC, in any class of membership.

Zimbabwe's Standards Association (SAZ) is listed on [ISO's member page as Zimbabwe's member body](<https://www.iso.org/member/308829.html>), as read in November 2026. The page shows 39 participating and 35 observing committee seats. In the last twelve months, SAZ's [list of standards published in the first quarter of 2026](<https://www.saz.org.zw/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Q1-published-standards-2026_-002.pdf>) added ISO/IEC standards on artificial intelligence, cloud security and digital evidence as national ones. Its [accreditations page](<https://www.saz.org.zw/accreditations-2/>), updated to February 2026, lists ZWS ISO/IEC 27001:2022 as a Zimbabwe Standard. No rule requiring public bodies to meet a named standard has been found. Operating would need a legal text that names an international standard on information technology or data and binds public bodies.
